title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction
title_zh: CompMVR：使用扩散模型的压缩感知多视图修复，实现几何一致的3D重建

paragraphs.en: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR , a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/ .

paragraphs.en: Modern 3D reconstruction models ( Kerbl et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Leroy et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) have achieved remarkable progress, yet most do not explicitly model compression artifacts that commonly appear in real-world visual inputs. In real-world deployments, however, visual inputs are frequently stored or transmitted in compressed forms, such as JPEG ( Wallace, 1991 ) , H.265/HEVC ( Sullivan et al., 2012 ) , and H.266/VVC ( Bross et al., 2021 ) . Existing compression artifact restoration methods ( Dehaghi et al., 2025 ) mainly formulate compression degradation at the frame level, aiming to recover high-fidelity visual appearance. Recently, latent diffusion-based models ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) have shown strong restoration capability by recovering image details degraded by lossy compression. Despite their effectiveness, existing methods remain largely image or video centric, without explicitly optimizing the multi-view geometric consistency required for 3D reconstruction. As shown in Fig. 1 , restoration can substantially affect the reliability of cross-view feature matching. However, this geometric aspect has been largely overlooked in prior restoration methods.

paragraphs.en: Recent diffusion-based restoration methods ( Lin et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2024 ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) have demonstrated strong generative priors for recovering perceptually realistic image details. They have been successfully explored for blind image restoration ( Lin et al., 2024 ) , real-world image super-resolution ( Wu et al., 2024 ) , photo-realistic image restoration ( Yu et al., 2024 ) , and compression artifact removal ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . However, these methods are primarily formulated as image or video restoration problems, where the goal is to improve visual fidelity, perceptual quality, or artifact reduction. When such methods are applied to compressed multi-view observations, restoration is typically performed in a view-wise manner. As a result, they do not explicitly enforce cross-view geometric consistency (see Tab. 1 ), which is essential for reliable correspondence estimation and downstream 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs.en: Motivated by these limitations, we newly propose CompMVR , a compression-aware multi-view restoration diffusion framework designed to improve geometric reliability for downstream 3D reconstruction. Our key observation is that compressed multi-view inputs can exhibit compression-induced inconsistency across views: artifacts depend on both the codec and QP, and thus may unsettle geometry-sensitive cues differently across views. To analyze this failure systematically, we construct a compressed multi-view benchmark by synthesizing compressed versions of existing 3D datasets under multiple codecs and quantization levels, while preserving codec and QP annotations. CompMVR uses codec and QP supervision during training, while inferring compression cues directly from the input at inference. Our benchmark shows that compression can substantially degrade geometry-sensitive tasks, including novel view synthesis, view matching, and camera pose estimation.

paragraphs.en: To address the challenge of handling view-dependent and spatially varying compression artifacts, CompMVR adopts a two-stage restoration framework for compressed multi-view inputs. In the first stage, CompMVR derives coding priors under codec and QP supervision during training via a compression prior embedder, explicitly characterizing the degradation regime for subsequent diffusion-based restoration. The coding priors provide the global compression context. In the second stage, the model introduces spatially varying artifact cues that capture the local reliability of geometry-critical regions, and jointly refines multiple views guided by these cues. To explicitly enforce geometric consistency, we incorporate correspondence-based supervision that aligns restoration across geometrically corresponding regions, while leveraging multi-view 3D attention to facilitate feature interaction across views. paragraphs.en: We propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion framework that integrates codec- and QP-conditioned global priors with spatially varying artifact estimation and correspondence-based supervision to improve cross-view geometric reliability during restoration.

paragraphs.en: We show consistent gains across image restoration metrics and downstream 2D/3D vision tasks, including feature matching, camera parameter estimation, point map prediction, novel-view synthesis, and 2D quality assessment with generalization across codecs and compression levels.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在图像复原指标及下游 2D/3D 视觉任务上展示了一致的提升，这些任务包括特征匹配、相机参数估计、点图预测、新视角合成，以及可在不同编解码器和压缩级别之间泛化的 2D 质量评估。

paragraphs.en: Recently, diffusion-based restoration methods ( Welker et al., 2024 ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) have shown notable performance in compression artifact removal. Compared with transformer-based models ( Liang et al., 2021 ; Zamir et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2022 ) , diffusion models provide generative priors through iterative denoising. CPGA ( Zhu et al., 2024 ) pioneers the use of explicit coding priors, such as motion vectors, residual frames, and predictive frames. More recent studies further incorporate degradation-related cues, such as quality factors, into diffusion-based restoration ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . These approaches demonstrate that explicit coding information can provide useful guidance for compression artifact removal. However, compression-aware restoration methods remain primarily focused on visual enhancement. Consequently, they do not explicitly optimize cross-view geometric reliability for downstream 3D reconstruction. Therefore, existing works remain largely geometry-agnostic, as they do not explicitly adapt restoration to the cross-view geometric requirements of downstream 3D reconstruction. In contrast, our work integrates explicit coding priors with cross-view diffusion restoration to recover geometry-consistent visual evidence from compressed multi-view inputs.

paragraphs.en: Diffusion-based models have been widely investigated for 3D reconstruction ( Liu et al., 2023 ; Poole et al., 2023 ; Lin et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023b ; Shi et al., 2024 ; Long et al., 2024 ; Gao et al., 2024 ) . Recently, rather than training generative models from scratch, many approaches adapt large-scale pretrained diffusion backbones, such as Stable Diffusion ( Rombach et al., 2022 ) , to provide strong visual priors for 3D-related tasks. In image-to-3D reconstruction, diffusion priors are often used to synthesize unseen viewpoints or enrich missing visual details under sparse or ambiguous observations ( Liu et al., 2023 ; Poole et al., 2023 ; Lin et al., 2023 ; Wang et al., 2023b ) . Several multi-view diffusion methods further extend image diffusion architectures by generating or refining multiple views jointly, often introducing 3D-aware attention mechanisms to encourage view consistency ( Shi et al., 2024 ; Long et al., 2024 ; Gao et al., 2024 ) . These designs demonstrate that diffusion priors can provide useful structural and appearance cues when observations are incomplete or constrained. However, most existing 3D reconstruction methods do not explicitly consider degradation types. To preserve cross-view consistency, SIR-Diff ( Mao et al., 2025 ) states that independent single-view restoration can compromise geometric constraints and processes multiple views jointly with a 3D self-attention transformer. However, SIR-Diff is not designed for compression-aware restoration, as it does not exploit codec- or QP-dependent coding priors that characterize compression artifacts. In contrast, our work studies diffusion priors under practical compression degradation and aims to recover geometry-consistent multi-view evidence for robust 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs.en: Recent 3D reconstruction methods have explored novel-view synthesis under degraded observations ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2023 ; Feng et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2023b ; Pearl et al., 2022 ; Zhou et al., 2023a ) . DIFIX3D+ ( Wu et al., 2025 ) uses diffusion priors to enhance artifact-contaminated NeRF/3DGS renderings, while HQGS ( Lin et al., 2025 ) studies robust 3DGS under degraded observations and CLIPGaussian ( Cao et al., 2025 ) incorporates semantic guidance and 3D spatial consistency for low-quality inputs. Other works address specific degradations such as extreme motion blur to improve camera estimation, geometry recovery, and reconstruction ( Jang et al., 2025 ) . Collectively, these studies show that degradation affects both visual quality and 3D geometry. However, they focus primarily on generic low-quality inputs, rendering artifacts, or specific capture degradations rather than codec-dependent compression in multi-view observations. In contrast, CompMVR explicitly models input-side lossy compression with compression-aware priors and cross-view supervision to improve geometric reliability before downstream 3D reconstruction.

paragraphs.en: We explicitly model spatially varying, content-dependent degradation within each view. While Stage 1 captures global compression characteristics such as codec type and QP, these signals cannot fully describe local artifact variations. To quantify this, we use a gradient-based energy function, e ⁡ ( I ) = | ∂ x I | + | ∂ y I | e(I)=|\partial_{x}I|+|\partial_{y}I| , defined as the L ​ 1 L1 norm of image gradients and commonly used in seam carving ( Avidan and Shamir, 2023 ) . Low-energy regions correspond to smooth areas, whereas high-energy regions capture texture-rich or edge-dominant structures. As shown in Fig. 3 , the energy map strongly correlates with the artifact map, with high-complexity regions exhibiting larger residuals than smooth regions even under identical QP settings. This shows that compression distortion depends not only on global parameters but also on local image structure, motivating explicit spatial degradation modeling.

paragraphs.en: Maintaining consistency across views is crucial for geometrically coherent restoration. Unlike video diffusion models designed for sequential frames with small viewpoint changes ( Dehaghi et al., 2025 ) , multi-view images exhibit large viewpoint disparities, where corresponding regions are geometrically displaced. As shown in Fig. 4 , applying a video diffusion model out of the box leads to view-inconsistent artifacts. This observation clearly demonstrates the necessity of geometry-aware consistency modeling for multi-view restoration. This challenge arises from the difficulty of establishing reliable correspondences under large viewpoint changes, occlusions, and view-dependent artifacts. Therefore, a robust mechanism for estimating geometry-aware correspondences is essential for enforcing cross-view consistency.
paragraphs.zh: 在多个视图之间保持一致性对于几何连贯的复原至关重要。 与为视点变化较小的连续帧设计的视频扩散模型（Dehaghi 等，2025）不同，多视图图像表现出较大的视点差异，其中对应区域在几何上发生了位移。 如图 4 所示，直接使用现成的视频扩散模型会导致视图不一致的伪影。 这一观察清楚地表明，对于多视图复原而言，几何感知的一致性建模是必不可少的。 这一挑战源于在大幅视点变化、遮挡以及视图相关伪影的情况下难以建立可靠的对应关系。 因此，一个用于估计几何感知对应关系的鲁棒机制，对于实施跨视图一致性至关重要。

paragraphs.en: We further incorporate Spatial-3D ResNet ( Mao et al., 2025 ; Shi et al., 2024 ) and 3D self-attention layers ( Mao et al., 2025 ) to model cross-view interactions, following prior multi-view diffusion approaches. Unlike SIR-Diff, which initializes the 3D modules from pre-trained Stable Video Diffusion (SVD) weights, we train all 3D components from scratch using zero initialization to avoid introducing temporal continuity priors that are not well aligned with multi-view image settings. These 3D layers enable implicit cross-view interaction by jointly modeling multi-view features. However, they do not explicitly model view-dependent degradation, as the attention mechanism is driven by feature similarity without an explicit notion of per-view quality. Our method complements this implicit modeling with explicit correspondence-based supervision in Eq. 8 , resulting in more robust multi-view consistency under view-varying compression artifacts.
paragraphs.zh: 我们进一步引入 Spatial-3D ResNet（Mao et al., 2025；Shi et al., 2024）和 3D 自注意力层（Mao et al., 2025）来建模跨视角交互，遵循以往的多视角扩散方法。 与 SIR-Diff 使用预训练的 Stable Video Diffusion（SVD）权重来初始化 3D 模块不同，我们采用零初始化从头训练所有 3D 组件，以避免引入与多视角图像场景不匹配的时间连续性先验。 这些 3D 层通过联合建模多视角特征，实现隐式的跨视角交互。 然而，它们并未显式地建模依赖视角的退化，因为注意力机制由特征相似性驱动，缺乏对每个视角质量的显式概念。 我们的方法通过公式 8 中基于对应关系的显式监督来补充这种隐式建模，从而在视角间变化的压缩伪影下获得更鲁棒的多视角一致性。

paragraphs.en: We compare CompMVR with CODiff ( Guo et al., 2025 ) , DiQP ( Dehaghi et al., 2025 ) , and the multi-view restoration model SIR-Diff ( Mao et al., 2025 ) . Tab. 7 shows that our method consistently achieves the best or second-best performance across 2D quality metrics under various codec and QP settings and remains robust under severe compression (e.g., QP 42). Fig. 6 further shows that existing methods often leave compression artifacts or over-smooth high-frequency structures, whereas CompMVR better preserves structural details and visual fidelity. paragraphs.en: We evaluate the impact of each Stage 2 component, including the compression prior from Stage 1, the compression artifact estimator (CAE) and the cross-view correspondence loss ℒ corr \mathcal{L}_{\text{corr}} . As shown in Tab. 12 , the compression prior alone provides competitive performance, while combining it with either CAE or ℒ corr \mathcal{L}_{\text{corr}} generally improves perceptual quality. However, the gains from the compression prior are modest and metric-dependent, indicating that it provides a complementary rather than dominant contribution to Stage 2. Nevertheless, using all three components yields the most balanced performance, achieving the best or second-best results across most metrics. The geometry-focused ablation in Tab. 12 further isolates the effect of correspondence supervision. paragraphs.en: As reported in Tab. 13 , our framework requires additional computation and GPU memory, and it is not yet a fully feed-forward pipeline. paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduce CompMVR , a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework designed to improve geometric reliability for downstream 3D reconstruction. Our method leverages coding priors and cross-view supervision to restore geometrically reliable multi-view inputs. Through extensive experiments across multiple codecs and QP settings, our results demonstrate that CompMVR improves novel-view synthesis and multiple downstream geometric tasks. Our results show that compression artifacts affect downstream 3D reconstruction, and that the restoration process should consider geometric reliability when targeting 3D vision applications.
